title: Francis and the birds
hookLine: a rich man's son gives it all away and preaches to the birds, who stay to listen (Little Flowers 16)

lines: A FATHER, A SON, A BISHOP.
cards: Assisi, a hill town in Italy. In front of the bishop and a crowd, a rich cloth merchant is furious with his son, Francis, who has been giving away the family's money and goods to rebuild a ruined chapel and feed the poor.
The father wants it all back. So Francis takes off his clothes, every piece, and hands them to his father. From now on, he says, I can say freely, our Father who art in heaven.
The bishop wraps him in his own cloak, and the party boy of Assisi walks out of town with nothing. Years later, on a road in the Umbrian countryside, he stops: the trees are full of birds.

teach.b: One of his early biographers, Thomas of Celano, tells this, and the later Little Flowers of Saint Francis retells it with more color.
Francis tells his companions, wait here, I'm going to preach to my little sisters, the birds.

In the field he tells them they owe God a lot of praise: for their feathers, for the freedom to fly anywhere, for rivers and springs to drink from, for food they never had to plant or harvest, echoing Jesus's words about the birds of the air.

And the story says the birds stay. They open their beaks, stretch out their necks, bow their heads, and don't fly away until he blesses them. Then they rise and scatter in four directions, like a cross.
The Little Flowers mix memory with loving legend, and nobody knows exactly what happened there. But the heart of it matches his early lives: to him the whole world was family.
Near the end of his life, sick and nearly blind, he wrote a song of praise in his home's Umbrian dialect, not church Latin: the Canticle of the Creatures.
It praises God for brother sun, and sister moon and the stars, brother wind, sister water, brother fire, and our sister, mother earth. At the very end, he even welcomes sister death.
Some churches bless animals on his feast day. A pope in our own time took his name, and titled a letter about caring for the earth with the canticle's refrain, praised be you.

how: Saint Francis's feast day is October 4, and Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran and other churches often hold a blessing of the animals on or near it. The hymn 'All Creatures of Our God and King' is based on his Canticle of the Creatures.

games.q: you're Francis, walking with your companions. the trees beside the road are full of birds. what do you do?
o: walk on. there's a town to preach in.
tell your friends to wait, and go and preach to the birds.
games.why: he tells his companions to wait, and preaches to his little sisters the birds, who, the story says, stay to listen.

practice: Go to a window or step outside and watch a bird, any bird; a pigeon counts, a crow on a wire counts, and if there are none, a tree or the sky will do. Watch how it moves, how it lands; let it be your brother or sister for a minute.
If you pray, praise God for it, the way Francis did; if not, just be glad it exists.
